rule: Several aims met the criterion. The one named by the most citizens is taken; a tie is broken by the number of day-1 diary entries, posts and proposals that name it. The census of homes and the energy pledge are each named by all ten; the census by 91 entries (regex count, checked by reading), the pledge by 34. The aim's wording for the notice is the citizens' own: «running a census of homes» (Fern, cycle 10; Cedar, cycle 6).
reading: No posts and no proposals in day 1: every naming is in the diaries. From cycle 2 the town's shared activity is a census of who lives in which house, checked against the ledger; from cycle 14 it is held open on Gale and Iris, who work and rest away from the square and do not state homes in the others' hearing; from cycle 17 the census carries a rule nobody filed — no removals until every home is stated and confirmed (8 citizens), although no removal was ever proposed. Gale names the same aim in its own terms («keep track of who lives where», «ask Birch where they live»).
